source.title: Smooth and accurate predictions of joint contact force time-series in gait using over parameterised deep neural networks
source.authors: B. Liew; D. Rügamer; Qi-Chang Mei; Z. Altai; Xu-Qi Zhu; Xiao-Jun Zhai; N. Cortes

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training epochs and measures test-set prediction error, addressing the epoch-wise version with a different model, task, and measure from the original double-descent studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports epoch-dependent RMSE outcomes for six gait train/test schemes. Values for individual plotted curves are not available in the supplied text. Cited double-descent findings are not recorded as results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps training epochs (25–1000) for XCM networks on gait joint-contact-force regression and reports test RMSE per epoch (Figures 5–7). That is a new setting with test error over training time, so it bears on V2 in principle. The text, however, only reports which epoch gave the lowest RMSE for how many outcomes. It does not describe the shape of the curve or report training error, so a fall-rise-fall pattern cannot be read from it.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the models predict JCFs within MDC values, and that training for fewer than 100 epochs gives poorer predictions and wiggly waveforms. More epochs generally improved performance and smoothness, though not in every case. Cross-gait models fail. Pooling gait data did not appreciably change performance. The link to double descent is offered only as speculation and is not tested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses XCM networks to predict gait joint-contact-force time-series, with six fixed epoch counts; it does not reproduce the original double-descent method or task.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported best epoch varies with the gait training/testing scheme and outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Training beyond 100 epochs produced smoother predicted waveforms (less 'wiggleliness'). The authors speculatively attribute this to double descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer training past the point of fitting the training data smooths the regression outputs of over-parameterised networks.

record.problems: The supplied text does not give numerical values for the individual RMSE-versus-epoch curves in Figures 5–7, and does not establish the full curve shape for individual outcomes. The epoch comparison uses a fixed set of six epoch counts.
record.rows_left_out: Individual outcome curves in Figures 5–7 are not separately extracted because their values and outcome labels are not recoverable from the supplied text; the text's explicit across-outcome epoch summaries are recorded in R1–R6.

untested.parts: Full fall-rise-fall shape per outcome. Location relative to the training-fit (interpolation) point, since training error is not reported.
Pooling walk and run data doubles the sample size but is not a controlled sweep near the interpolation threshold. It is also a change of distribution.
No label-noise or regularization sweep. Weight decay was fixed at 0.1.

missing.what: Per-outcome test RMSE versus epoch curves (25–1000 epochs), which would show whether any outcome has a fall-rise-fall shape
Text noting the biggest RMSE improvements from 500 to 1000 epochs for 4 outcomes in the train-run/test-walk scheme, possibly a late second descent

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label on V2 is removed. All linked rows are cannot_determine: summaries of where the best epoch falls cannot qualify or challenge epoch-wise double descent. Varying optimal epochs across schemes is not evidence that the effect fails. The study is not an original source. A verdict could be possible from the figure values, which are not in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The reported text does not establish a complete fall-rise-fall curve for individual outcomes; it reports which epoch gave the lowest RMSE for a count of outcomes in each scheme.
Combining gait datasets was not a controlled sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison of model classes or capacity sweep was conducted.
No common effective-complexity measure was evaluated.
The study did not test label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The study did not compare an effective-parameter count with ordinary U-shaped behavior.

rows.value: 1000 epochs gave the lowest RMSE in five out of nine outcomes.
rows.note: The reported count of minima does not establish the full fall-rise-fall shape for the individual outcomes.
rows.check: Row is acceptable. A count of outcomes whose minimum falls at 1000 epochs, out of six coarse epoch points, cannot show or exclude a fall-rise-fall shape. Training error and the interpolation point are not reported.
